_source: The Town Hall's rooms. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-29: a new location on the street, the Town Hall, with a Fishbowl for community fishbowl meetings open to anybody with CB access, and rooms for the Stimpunks Directors, Board Members and Moderators, which anybody can walk into and whose CB only shows for people signed on with the moderators' password (the base). Every `what` is Ryan's own sentence from the brief, word for word, and the rooms are in his order. Which rooms are private is NOT decided here: it is MOD_ROOMS in netlify/cb/lib.mjs, the one list the server checks, and tools/make-town-hall.py refuses this file if its `for` disagrees with that list. A room with no page yet is on the rotunda's wall as a door not open yet, which is the campgrounds' raising state: named, not dimmed, not a link.
_roles: Ryan's next step, not built yet: a list of MOD handles, each with roles (moderator, board, director, administrator), so that the Board room is for the board role, the Directors room for the director role, the Moderators room for any MOD, and an administrator for everything. When it arrives, `for` becomes the role a room needs, and MOD_ROOMS in lib.mjs becomes a map from room to role. See DECISIONS.md.

lede: Clear governance, transparent leadership, and documented organizational structure are essential to accountability. The following pages provide essential information about our legal status, board composition, financial oversight, and institutional policies.
Accountability starts with governance, oversight, and clear ethical commitments.

items.name: Frequently Requested Information
items.note: Legal status, EIN, board and staff composition, funding overview, and core organizational facts.

items.name: Bylaws
items.note: The rules that govern how we are run, published in full. The version shown is the one proposed for adoption at our September 2026 board meeting, with the family qualification for directors removed from §2.1.

items.name: Board Roles & Responsibilities
items.note: What we ask of a director, what we deliberately do not ask — no give-or-get, no travel, no performing wellness — what each officer does, and what the Foundation owes its board in return.

close: Governance is not bureaucracy. Governance is how we keep the commons safe and durable.
Our governance model is grounded in lived experience leadership and epistemic justice, ensuring decision-making reflects the communities most impacted by the systems we seek to redesign.
governance._dropped: The page links "epistemic justice" to /philosophy/epistemic-justice/, which answered 404 on 2026-09-29, and stimpunks.org has no page by that name (the glossary has Epistemic Injustice). The words are kept as the page has them and the dead link is left off; the link is stimpunks.org's to fix.

_people: A room may list who it is for. Each person links to their own section of stimpunks.org/about/, and the list is in the order, and with the titles, of the page named in `people_from` (the About page's Directors and Board Members section for the Directors, at Ryan's ask, 2026-09-29; the Board Governance page's Board of Directors for the Board, which is the page that says who is on it and that the people who run the work day to day are not). tools/make-town-hall.py checks every name against the Knowledge System mirror's copy of the page it came from, and every anchor against the mirror's About page, when the mirror is on this machine, and refuses what has gone; the anchors were also checked on the live pages on 2026-09-29. Nothing here is typed from memory: when either page changes, re-read it.
_governance: A room may carry a section of one of our own stimpunks.org pages, word for word, at Ryan's ask: the Board room carries the Governance & Ethics section of our Accountability & Transparency page (2026-09-29). Every sentence and every link here is that page's, copied as it stands, with its relative links made absolute; tools/make-town-hall.py looks for every one of them in the Knowledge System mirror's copy of the page when the mirror is on this machine, and refuses one that has gone. When the page changes, re-copy the section; never loosen the check. The Bylaws line names the September 2026 board meeting, so it will change once the Board votes.
